blockers.description: SQL Server DENY/GRANT/REVOKE cannot target the executing principal itself — upfix_app could not DENY permissions to itself for migration 006
blockers.workaround: Resolved: applied CREATE TABLE + DENY for migration 006 as sa (a separate admin principal), then manually inserted the schema_migrations tracking row. This is expected SQL Server behavior, not a bug — future migrations issuing DENY/GRANT/REVOKE against the app's own login must run the same way, via an admin credential, not via bin/migrate.php's normal upfix_app connection.

decisions.decision: Live SQL Server instance provisioned at 10.209.30.97:1433 (SQL Server 2019 Express), database upfix created, login/user upfix_app created
decisions.rationale: No local SQL Server/Docker/sudo available in this WSL environment; user supplied a remote instance instead

decisions.decision: upfix_app granted db_datareader + db_datawriter + db_ddladmin + db_securityadmin (NOT db_owner, NOT sysadmin)
decisions.rationale: Narrowest role set that still lets bin/migrate.php run DDL and issue DENY/GRANT for other principals; deliberately avoids incidental rights like ALTER DATABASE/backup permissions; DENY still overrides any GRANT this role membership implies, per SQL Server permission precedence, so AUDIT-01's guarantee is not weakened

decisions.decision: TrustServerCertificate=true and LoginTimeout hardcoded into Connection.php's DSN string builder (not a new .env key)
decisions.rationale: User-specified pattern; this SQL Server instance uses a self-signed/default cert
